message.content:
Lion (Panthera leo) and zebra (Equus quagga) belong to very different orders—Carnivora and Perissodactyla, respectively.  
Their most recent common ancestor is therefore the last common ancestor of those two orders, which is a small, insectivorous placental mammal that lived roughly **70 million years ago**. In other words, they share a common ancestor in the clade of placental mammals that gave rise to the orders Carnivora and Perissodactyla.
